newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude prices fall in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude prices fall in lackluster trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell Wednesday, amid lackluster local trade and steady markets in other regions, traders said.
Sales of Alaska North Slope (ANs) crude -- the West Coast regional benchmark -- remained flat. Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI)
Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude fell to $17.32/17.49 a barrel.
Light Line 63 crude also weakened with spot WTI, while its discount remained steady at minus $3.05 a barrel, and its price over Buena Vista stood unchanged at 90 cents to $1.00.
State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) sold a 360,000 barrel cargo of Maya heavy crude to a Los Angeles refinery late last week, market sources said.

At least four other refiners, including Shell, Texaco, Mobil and Ultramar are in line to take delivery of Maya totaling about 1.7 million barrels over the next two months. Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- were flat after major oil companies lowered postings late Monday.
